# @jpisgeek/documentation-evidence

Captures fixed operational metadata v1 from versioned stored Swamp resources.
Includes the infrastructure-guide model-scope report. There is no arbitrary
field selection, generic scalar projection, label, description or free-text
payload. Counts, nullable boolean flags, an enumerated collector outcome and an
original observation timestamp are the entire producer contract. This is a
deliberate replacement for the unpublished projection draft, not a drop-in
adapter for raw collector resources. Its sibling @jpisgeek/inventory-coverage is
also an intentionally public MIT extension in this repository; this is a public
package identity, not a private deployment or workflow name.

**Version** `2026.10.14.1` · **License** MIT · **Source**
https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/tree/documentation-evidence-2026.10.14.1/documentation-evidence

## Install

```
swamp extension pull @jpisgeek/documentation-evidence
```

## `@jpisgeek/documentation-evidence`

### Arguments

| argument              | type                                                                                     | required | default | description |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `sources`             | array of object                                                                          | yes      |         |             |
| `sources[].category`  | `compute` \| `storage` \| `network` \| `applications` \| `automation` \| `documentation` | yes      |         |             |
| `sources[].modelType` | string                                                                                   | yes      |         |             |
| `sources[].modelId`   | string                                                                                   | yes      |         |             |
| `sources[].dataName`  | string                                                                                   | yes      |         |             |

### Methods

#### `capture`

Validate operational metadata v1 from existing stored resources; no arbitrary
projections

No arguments.

### Data written

| resource   | lifetime | fields                        | description                                                                    |
| ---------- | -------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `snapshot` | 30d      | `collectedAt`, `observations` | Fixed operational metadata with original observation times and pinned versions |

## Example

```yaml
globalArguments:
  sources:
    - category: storage
      modelType: "@example/operational-metadata"
      modelId: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
      dataName: summary
reports:
  require:
    - "@jpisgeek/infrastructure-guide"
```

## Caveats

A trusted producer must write exactly this JSON contract (all keys required):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "observedAt": "2026-10-14T12:00:00.123Z",
  "collectorStatus": "succeeded",
  "counts": { "expected": 9, "observed": 7, "unhealthy": 2, "unknown": 1 },
  "flags": { "reachable": false, "configured": null }
}
```

`collectorStatus` is `succeeded`, `failed` or `unknown`. It describes the
producer's declared outcome, not a verified latest run. Counts are integers from
0 through 1,000,000. Observed cannot exceed expected; unhealthy plus unknown
cannot exceed observed (these are disjoint observed subsets). Unobserved
expected items are expected minus observed. Flags are booleans or null
(unknown). `observedAt` is null or a valid UTC ISO timestamp with exactly three
fractional-second digits. No fallback to resource creation/capture time. Future
times are retained, never treated as fresh by @jpisgeek/inventory-coverage.
Extra or missing keys at every object level, unsupported values, coercion,
arbitrary selectors and free-text labels are rejected, not silently stripped.

Run `capture` against an existing producer; it writes one `snapshot` with
`collectedAt` and observations. The latest exact named version is pinned;
unrelated resources are not enumerated. A missing/deleted/empty resource is
unavailable with null metadata, never a healthy zero. Malformed evidence,
repository failures, missing/invalid size metadata or invalid versions fail the
whole capture before writing any partial snapshot. The report reads only this
successful execution's exact snapshot version and renders from validated fields;
no older/latest fallback.

Categories are compute, storage, network, applications, automation and
documentation, one source per category (1-6 total). Source model IDs are UUIDs;
types use slash-separated ASCII identifier segments. Resource names are 1-200
ASCII letters/digits/dot/colon/underscore/hyphen, starting alphanumeric. These
are storage routes, not shell paths. Routing identifiers stay in the
configuration and are not copied to snapshots/reports. Exact-name metadata
lookup rejects rename redirects; the configured UUID must match its model type.
Recorded size must be an integer from 0 to 64,000 before streaming begins.
Source/report streams accumulate at most 64,000 bytes in this extension;
overflow or a byte count differing from recorded size fails without truncation.
This is NOT a whole-platform allocation bound: Swamp may buffer metadata, scan
definitions to resolve a UUID, enumerate versions when a latest marker is
absent, hydrate content or buffer remote-worker artifacts before yielding. The
Swamp repository/backend and its metadata writers are trusted; do not run
against attacker-controlled storage. Backend resource quotas/isolation are the
operator's responsibility, not provided by this schema. Locally tested with the
filesystem backend; remote-worker and hydration allocation are not tested or
claimed bounded. Malformed UTF-8/JSON fails. Requires context
definitionRepository.findByIdGlobal plus dataRepository.findByName and stream;
unsupported contexts fail rather than falling back to unbounded reads. Numeric
JSON must survive decimal round-trip; rounded, underflowed, non-finite and
negative-zero values fail closed. Numeric parsing requires JSON reviver
source-context support. Snapshots retain 30 days and at most 30 versions. This
pure data pipeline is tested on macOS ARM64 and Linux x86_64; it does not assert
any backend's platform compatibility.

## Security

No network, subprocess, environment or vault access. Only configured stored
resources are read through Swamp's repository. No private data is automatically
published. Strict schema validation reduces the accepted data surface; it is NOT
a universal secret detector or proof of truthful producer data. An authorized
writer could encode information in valid numbers/timestamps/flags. Review and
trust producers and protect configuration, observations, snapshots and both
report formats as operational data. Do not use configuration routing fields as
secret storage. No arbitrary source text is rendered; error details are
sanitized and cancellation remains cancellation. Adding an adapter for a raw
collector requires its own explicit reviewed mapping, never a generic
field-selecting escape hatch. MIT shared contract code is bundled into the
@jpisgeek/inventory-coverage package, requiring no live grant or separate
runtime install.

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jpisgeek/slog-bog/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
for the release gates every version passes before it reaches the registry.
